'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]], [[War against the Islamic State]]
**[[Islamic State insurgency in Puntland]]
***[[Puntland Security Force|Puntland forces]] carry out [[Drone warfare|drone strikes]] on [[Islamic State – Somalia Province|Islamic State]] targets in the [[Cal Miskaad]] mountains near [[Balidhidhin District]], [[Bari, Somalia|Bari]], [[Puntland]], [[Somalia]], killing several militants. [https://www.idilnews.com/puntland-forces-conduct-airstrikes-on-isis-positions-around-balodhidin-of-bari-region/ (Idil News)] [https://www.voasomali.com/a/duqeymo-ka-dhacay-degaano-ka-mid-ah-gobolka-bari/7931018.html (VOA)]
***Puntland [[counterterrorism]] forces capture four foreign Islamic State fighters from [[Ethiopia]], [[Yemen]], and [[Tanzania]], while intercepting and destroying multiple explosive-carrying drones in Bari, Puntland. [https://www.idilnews.com/puntland-forces-conduct-airstrikes-on-isis-positions-around-balodhidin-of-bari-region/ (Idil News)] [https://www.voasomali.com/a/duqeymo-ka-dhacay-degaano-ka-mid-ah-gobolka-bari/7931018.html (VOA)] [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/puntland/islamic-state-foreign-fighters-surrender-in-somalia-s-puntland-amid-offensive (Garowe Online)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Israeli Air Force|Israeli airstrikes]] across the [[Gaza Strip]] kill at least 22 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/1/9/live-israel-kills-50-people-in-gaza-recovers-body-of-captive-from-rafah (Al Jazeera)]
**A study published in ''[[The Lancet]]'' claims that around 3% of the Gaza Strip population has died from traumatic injury due to the conflict with Israel, with the death toll from other causes due to the military campaign likely higher. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/01/09/middleeast/gaza-death-toll-underreported-study-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[artillery]] strikes kill two people in [[Siversk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], according to the region's governor. In the Russian-controlled area of [[Kamianka-Dniprovska]], [[Zaporizhzhia Oblast]], Ukraine, the region's Russia-appointed governor says that two people were killed by Ukrainian artillery strikes. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/four-dead-shelling-incidents-ukraine-officials-say-2025-01-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 California wildfires]]
**[[January 2025 Southern California wildfires]]
***At least six people are killed due to spreading [[Wildfire|wildfires]] in [[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]], [[United States]]. 
*** The Kenneth Fire ignites in [[Woodland Hills, Los Angeles|Woodland Hills]], adding to the 179,000 people placed under evacuation orders. [https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/wildfires/live-blog/california-wildfires-live-updates-deadly-blazes-spread-hollywood-hills-rcna186927 (NBC News)]
*[[2024–25 European winter]]
**Two people are killed and 20 others are injured in a [[Winter storm|snowstorm]] in northern [[France]]. [https://apnews.com/article/france-europe-cold-snap-snow-weather-deaths-eb1cd5d181c6ce4b8ca32b5e8e29b727 (AP)]
*Twelve [[miner]]s are trapped in a collapsed [[coal mine]] in [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], following a [[methane]] [[gas explosion]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-coal-miners-trapped-southwest-5befdfc30cdda20919a3ad74acd2c6dd (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Armenia–European Union relations]]
**The [[Government of Armenia|Armenian government]] approves a bill to launch a bid for [[Armenia|the country]] to join the [[European Union]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/armenian-government-approves-bill-launch-eu-accession-bid-2025-01-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[Azerbaijan–Russia relations]]
**[[Russia]] declines to confirm whether [[Air and Missile Defense Forces|Russian forces]] accidentally shot down [[Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243]], despite calls by [[Azerbaijan]] to do so. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/kremlin-declines-to-accept-responsibility-for-plane-crash (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Guyana–Venezuela territorial dispute]]
**[[Guyana]] says that it will resort to the [[United Nations]] to deter [[Venezuela]] from unilaterally appointing a governor for the [[Regions of Guyana|Essequibo]], a region under Guyanese control but claimed by Venezuela. [https://apnews.com/article/guyana-venezuela-un-top-court-essequibo-ae871c1b8514d555aed9f6182207466f (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[International Criminal Court arrest warrants for Israeli leaders]]
**[[Poland]]'s government confirms that it will not comply with an [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC) warrant to arrest [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] for [[war crime]]s if he chooses to attend a ceremony at [[Auschwitz concentration camp]] later this month. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/polish-president-seeks-to-shield-netanyahu-as-warrant-scuppers-auschwitz-memorial-visit/ (''Times of Israel'')] [https://notesfrompoland.com/2025/01/09/poland-confirms-it-will-not-arrest-netanyahu-on-icc-warrant-if-he-attends-auschwitz-anniversary/ (Notes from Poland)]
**The [[U.S. House of Representatives]] votes 243 to 140 to sanction the ICC for issuing arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and former [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli Defense Minister]] [[Yoav Gallant]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-house-votes-sanction-international-criminal-court-over-israel-2025-01-09/ (Reuters)] [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/us-lawmakers-vote-sanction-icc-officials-issuing-netanyahu-warrant (Middle East Eye)] [https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2025-01-09/ty-article/.premium/u-s-house-votes-to-sanction-icc-over-alleged-targeting-of-senior-israeli-officials/00000194-4c7e-d6f4-a9b5-5cfe67660000 (''Haaretz'')]
**[[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] [[Party leaders of the United States Senate|majority leader]] [[John Thune]] promises swift consideration of the Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act so [[President of the United States|President-elect]] [[Donald Trump]] can sign it into law shortly after [[Second inauguration of Donald Trump|taking office]]. Under the act, any foreigner who investigates, arrests, detains or prosecutes [[U.S. citizens]] or those of an allied country, including Israel, not under ICC jurisdiction would be sanctioned along with their family members. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-house-votes-sanction-international-criminal-court-over-israel-2025-01-09/ (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/09/us/politics/icc-sanctions-house-israel.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2024 Venezuelan political crisis]]
**[[Venezuela]]n [[Venezuelan opposition|opposition]] leader [[María Corina Machado]] makes her first public appearance in 133 days and is briefly arrested when her convoy is intercepted by [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|security forces]] as it departs an anti-government protest in [[Caracas]]. The incident occurs the day before the ruling party-controlled [[National Assembly of Venezuela|National Assembly]] is scheduled to swear in [[Nicolás Maduro]] for a third term as [[President of Venezuela|president]]. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-election-inauguration-maduro-protests-edmundo-machado-db8a045f2614cb71022674dc6b73bd88 (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jan/09/venezuela-maria-corina-machado-kidnapped (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] bans [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] from operating in the country and revokes its [[press credentials]], citing the network's interview with [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebel]] leader [[Bertrand Bisimwa]] as an [[Al Jazeera controversies and criticism|endorsement of terrorism]]. Authorities warn against reporting on the group, with the [[Ministry of Justice (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|justice minister]] threatening to invoke the [[Capital punishment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo|death penalty]], although no [[Constitution of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|formal law]] bans such [[Mass media in the Democratic Republic of the Congo|coverage]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-al-jazeera-ban-92871abe63d84f798ecf6d229e6f74de (AP)]
*The [[Kuwait]]i public prosecution detains media personality [[Fajer Al-Saeed]] for 21 days and after investigating charges related to "calling for normalization with the [[Israel]]i occupation and harming the state's interests". [https://www.aljazeera.net/misc/2025/1/9/%D8%A8%D8%AA%D9%87%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%B7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%B9-%D8%B3%D8%AC%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%A9 (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Mozambican general election]]
**[[2024 Mozambican protests]]
***[[Optimist Party for the Development of Mozambique|PODEMOS]] [[President of Mozambique|presidential]] candidate [[Venâncio Mondlane]], who alleges that the October election was [[Electoral fraud|rigged]], returns to [[Mozambique]] from exile in [[South Africa]] amid protests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mozambique-opposition-leader-returns-after-fleeing-post-election-safety-fears-2025-01-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022–2025 Lebanese presidential election]]
**[[Lebanese Armed Forces|Military]] [[Commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces|commander]] [[Joseph Aoun]] is elected as [[President of Lebanon]], ending the [[power vacuum]] that began in October 2022. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-parliament-president-joseph-aoun-hezbollah-942ce2e5d5619f072c8b23850ebce7b5 (AP)]
*[[Death and state funeral of Jimmy Carter]]
**The [[state funeral]] for former [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Jimmy Carter]] is held at the [[Washington National Cathedral|National Cathedral]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] All five living presidents, including incumbent president [[Joe Biden]] and [[President-elect of the United States|president-elect]] [[Donald Trump]], attend the funeral. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jimmy-carters-funeral-living-presidents-together-national-cathedral/ (CBS News)]
*[[President of São Tomé and Príncipe|President]] of [[São Tomé and Príncipe]] [[Carlos Vila Nova]] rejects a proposal by his [[Independent Democratic Action]] party to elect Hélio Vaz de Almeida as [[Prime Minister of São Tomé and Príncipe|prime minister]]. Vila Nova instead appoints [[Ilza Amado Vaz]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/pt/%C3%A1frica-lus%C3%B3fona/20250109-presidente-rejeita-nome-de-h%C3%A9lio-vaz-de-almeida-para-primeiro-ministro (RFI)], [https://english.news.cn/africa/20250110/8cb26230d24645d2ba4e9ff3d4ae696d/c.html (Xinhua)]
